title: Eisenkot ends Israeli consultations with 67 backers to Netanyahu's 46; Herzog to decide Sunday
dek: President Herzog says the result appears clear but mutual vetoes leave it unclear who can form a government. The Arab-led Joint List backed Eisenkot, and Likud called for a unity government.
author: Declaration Desk
body:
Opposition leader Gadi Eisenkot ended Israel's presidential consultations on Thursday with the backing of parties holding 67 of the Knesset's 120 seats, against 46 for Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, President Isaac Herzog said. Herzog said the results "appear clear" but that he would hold further one-on-one talks with party leaders before deciding, and intends to assign the mandate to form a government on Sunday, reports said.

Herzog said the vetoes that parties have placed on one another, both between and within the two blocs, made it unclear who could actually assemble a governing coalition. He said he would try to clarify the situation "directly and quickly". Eisenkot's Yashar party urged him to hand Eisenkot the mandate "as soon as possible", calling the 67 recommendations the largest number for any candidate since 2015 and describing Netanyahu as "a caretaker prime minister" without a majority.

## How the day ended

The Joint List, an alliance of Arab-led parties with 11 seats, decided unanimously to recommend Eisenkot, saying it was responding to "the public demand to prevent Netanyahu and his government from returning to power", according to reports. It told Herzog it would back an Eisenkot government from outside rather than join it, and would not help topple it. Its recommendation took Eisenkot past the 61 needed for a majority of the house.

Likud, the last party to meet Herzog, urged the opposition to end its boycott of Netanyahu and join a broad unity government. Likud MP Miri Regev called Eisenkot's camp a "disaster bloc"; Herzog replied, "If you want to extend a hand, you can't call it a 'disaster bloc'," according to one report. The same report said that Avigdor Liberman, whose Yisrael Beytenu backs Eisenkot, was willing to sit in government with United Torah Judaism, reversing his long-held position.

The ultra-Orthodox United Torah Judaism declined earlier in the day to recommend Netanyahu, or anyone else; it had backed him after each of the previous five elections, reports said.

## What happened

United Torah Judaism (UTJ) met Herzog first on Thursday morning. "We came to discuss topics and not people," its lawmaker Yitzhak Pindrus said, according to reports. The party's Degel HaTorah faction, which holds four of its seven seats, said on Wednesday it would recommend no one, on instructions from its rabbis, one report said. The report described the decision as a sign of the rift with Netanyahu over his government's failure to pass a law exempting religious seminary students from military service. Pindrus said the party's priority was "sorting out the status of Torah students", another report said.

Also on Thursday, the left-wing Democrats, led by Yair Golan, and the Arab-led Ra'am party of Mansour Abbas recommended Eisenkot. Abbas told Herzog his party supports fully disarming Hamas, reports said. The far-right Otzma Yehudit party of Itamar Ben-Gvir recommended Netanyahu, and its delegation repeated claims that the election was stolen. Naftali Bennett's B'Yachad, Yashar and Likud met Herzog later in the day.

On Wednesday the Religious Zionist Party, Shas and Zehut recommended Netanyahu, while Avigdor Liberman's Yisrael Beytenu backed Eisenkot.

## The numbers

Final results give Netanyahu's bloc 53 of the Knesset's 120 seats, the opposition camp 48, and the Arab-led lists 19, so no side has the 61 needed for a majority. Eisenkot's 67 recommendations combine the opposition camp's 48 seats with the 19 of the Arab-led lists. Netanyahu's 46 are his bloc's 53 minus the seven seats of United Torah Judaism.

Recommendations are not the same as a coalition. Eisenkot and his allies have said they will not form a government with the Arab-led parties, and Liberman could walk away if Eisenkot relied on their support, reports said. Several of his partners also oppose sitting with the ultra-Orthodox parties.

## Netanyahu's response

Netanyahu said in a video that there were "serious suspicions" that foreign powers had funded the election and questioned the loyalty of Arab citizens, reports said. Israel's Central Elections Committee certified the results on Wednesday and said it had found no evidence of fraud.

## What happens next

Herzog is not bound to choose the candidate with the most recommendations, and says he will announce his choice on Sunday. Whoever receives the mandate has 28 days to form a government, which can be extended by 14. The new Knesset is sworn in on 10 November.

For India, which has close defence, technology and trade ties with Israel, the outcome will shape Israeli policy on the stalled Gaza ceasefire and on Iran. Eisenkot has warned against a new war with Iran, which matters to India because of the risk to oil supplies and Indian seafarers in the Strait of Hormuz.
